topic: Deliberately NOT agreeing with 'nur noch ein Katzensprung' -- honest measurement of what the 100% actually proves, and a realistic gap list for a genuinely deployable Xeno module
instruction_context: Coordinator explicitly declined to endorse the owner's 'almost done' framing and asked for the same honesty here, rather than telling the framing back to it. This note follows that instruction.

part_1_novel_nontemplate_test.why_this_was_necessary: The 100% reported in RUN4_FINAL_100PCT_20260827.json is real and mechanically proven for the templated diagnostic curriculum -- but it says nothing about whether the trained 0.8B model itself generalizes, since 16 of 16 families are now answered by deterministic resolvers, not the model. Built 10 hand-written scenarios (legal/medical/scientific domains, implicit rather than stated branch counts, paraphrased rather than literal 'FORMALLY EXCLUDES' trigger phrasing, including a 5-branch case never seen in training) and ran them against the real run-3 model directly, live in the claylab sandbox -- not the resolver.
part_1_novel_nontemplate_test.result: 8/10 (80%) exactly correct. All 10 were shell-validated (real trained atoms, no format collapse) -- the format-reliability improvement from runs 2-3 held up on novel input even where correctness didn't.
part_1_novel_nontemplate_test.the_real_finding: Not random noise -- a specific, repeatable bias. Every case where PRESERVE_BRANCHES was correct: 7/7 right. Every case where COLLAPSE_VALID was correct (real excluding evidence, phrased in unfamiliar vocabulary): only 1/3 right, missing 2. The model appears to default to the cautious/conservative answer under novel phrasing rather than genuinely evaluating evidence strength -- it recognizes 'nothing has ruled this out' reliably, but under-recognizes 'this rules it out' when the exclusion isn't phrased with the training's literal trigger language ('formally excludes').
part_1_novel_nontemplate_test.epistemic_note: This specific bias (under-collapsing rather than over-collapsing) is the SAFER of the two possible failure directions given the project's own stated law ('majority does not collapse branches', collapsing should require real warrant) -- a false PRESERVE wastes an option, a false COLLAPSE improperly discards a live branch, which is the worse error for this system's actual purpose. Worth noting as a partial mitigant, not an excuse: 80% correct on a 10-case probe is still real evidence of an incomplete generalization, not proof the model 'basically has it'.
part_1_novel_nontemplate_test.raw_data: NOVEL_NONTEMPLATE_TEST_RESULTS_20260827.json in this packet directory -- all 10 cases, full raw model output, verdicts.

part_2_second_opinion.source: ~/last-resort/llm.py pool (Groq tier this call) -- ChatGPT bridge checked again before starting, still eingeloggt=false/0 cookies, not used.
part_2_second_opinion.reviewed_not_pasted_verbatim: The pool's answer was blunt and largely correct, but overstated one mechanism: it said the deterministic resolver would 'fail to fire or fire on the wrong pattern' on novel input. Checked directly against this session's own test suite (test_unrecognized_prompt_fails_closed_not_a_guess): the resolver/dispatcher explicitly FAILS CLOSED on unrecognized input (returns None, never guesses) -- that specific silent-wrong-answer risk applies to the MODEL's behavior on novel input (confirmed above: both novel-test misses were syntactically valid, shell-validated, confidently wrong atoms, not a refusal), not to the resolver, which was specifically built and tested to decline rather than misfire. Corrected in the summary below.
part_2_second_opinion.point_kept: The pool's core prioritization -- that the missing real tokenizer-bound atom manifest is the single most consequential remaining gap, since it blocks the entire vector-ABI/HRR layer the Master Spec describes as the actual long-term representation system -- matches this repo's own DoD document's independent ranking ('HRR artifact generation... the single highest-value next step, unblocks DoD points 1, 3, 7, 8 simultaneously') and is kept.

Everything trained in runs 1-3 used placeholder ABI_ACCEPTED_ORDINAL:NN strings, not real single-token bindings.

XENO_MODEL_SLOT/v1 production identity binding -- xeno_shell_model_slot_v1.py correctly requires a real measured checkpoint-identity receipt (vector-ABI binding, hook registry, loader receipt); the diagnostic wrapper built today explicitly does NOT satisfy this contract and says so in its own docstring. No production-grade model slot exists for today's trained checkpoint.
ZECP13/14 Claude Code bridge -- not built in any prior session, not touched today.
GLOBAL_WORKSPACE_REENTRY_RECEIPT_CONTRACT/v1 (proving a workspace broadcast was actually causally used, not just present) -- not built.

GRID10 / variable-N runtime re-verification -- physical GRID10 acceptance exists from a PRIOR session (not today's work); not re-run, re-verified, or extended today. The N-invariance cross-test against the existing grid10_logical_n_interface_v1.py sweep, flagged as 'not yet cross-tested' in the prior DoD, remains untested.

Coordinator leasing (ZECP11) integration -- the model slot module explicitly composes with existing grid10_fabric.py leasing rather than inventing its own, but this composition was never exercised end-to-end with today's trained model.
important_scope_clarification_on_todays_: The B6_GWT families' '100%' comes from regex-extracting scores directly out of a TEXT DESCRIPTION of a competition and computing argmax -- this proves the curriculum's textual encoding of GWT scoring is parseable. It does NOT prove or exercise a real, live, multi-node GWT competition/broadcast/uptake mechanism operating over actual candidate NODE_RESULT packets in a live S1 workspace, which is what ZECP10 actually describes.

The B6_DB_VS_SIM family's '100%' comes from detecting literal marker phrases in a templated text description ('SELECT against the canonical S0 ledger' etc.) -- it proves the curriculum's textual encoding of S0-vs-simulation is parseable. It does NOT prove the actual S0/S1/S2 state-transition machinery (xeno_shell_s0s1s2_transitions_v1.py) correctly discriminates real database reads from real simulation output in a live running system.

This is not a criticism of today's work -- the diagnostic curriculum was explicitly scoped as a curriculum, per its own METHOD_ONLY/training_eligible=false governance flags, never claimed to BE the live runtime. It is a reminder not to read '16/16 curriculum families solved' as '16/16 runtime capabilities proven' -- they are related but not the same claim.

honest_one_paragraph_summary: This is a real, verified, honest research checkpoint with clearly identified core gaps -- not a nearly-finished product. The 100% proven today is mechanically real and a genuine, useful result (every templated diagnostic case in this curriculum is now answered correctly and reliably, by construction), but it is a statement about the deterministic shell's coverage of a fixed curriculum, not a statement about the trained model's generalized reasoning ability, which measured at 80% on ten novel, non-templated scenarios today with a specific, real, systematic bias (under-recognizing genuine excluding evidence when phrased unfamiliarly). Separately and independently, the foundational production-grade pieces described in this project's own architecture spec -- a real tokenizer-bound atom manifest, measured HRR vector operations, a production model-slot identity binding, the Claude Code bridge, workspace-reentry proof, and a re-verified variable-N runtime -- remain not built, confirmed by direct filesystem checks rather than assumed. 'Ein Katzensprung' is not the honest description of the distance from here to a genuinely deployable Xeno module; 'a real foundation with several still-substantial, clearly enumerated pieces of work remaining' is.
